review_notes: I read the whole file. It defines three things: `uniqueHomsetOfInitialIsoUnit`, `uniqueHomsetOfZero` and `equivPUnit`. They build on existing Mathlib API (`Equiv.unique`, `Iso.homCongr`, `ihom.adjunction`, `Functor.star`, `Functor.fromPUnit`, `Functor.punitExt`). I grepped Mathlib for similar declarations. The closest hits were `Functor.equiv_punit_iff_unique` in Mathlib/CategoryTheory/PUnit.lean and the `Over`/`Under` equivalences with `Discrete PUnit` in Comma/Over/StrictInitial.lean. `equiv_punit_iff_unique` is a theorem, not a competing definition of the concept. It gives only `Nonempty`, so it doesn't provide the explicit equivalence that `equivPUnit` constructs. The `Over`/`Under` equivalences cover different categories. I found no independent definition of the same concept, so I'm abstaining.
